notes: The temperature sensor as the shared dependency of every other channel. The blast radius is stated most directly in the EPA SOP (epa-nist-temp-check-01: because the pH, dissolved oxygen, specific conductance and ORP probes all rely on the temperature sensor, each temperature sensor must be checked against a NIST-traceable thermometer; epa-solution-volume-01: the calibration solution must cover both the probe and the temperature sensor; epa-do-dry-sensor-01: evaporating moisture on the temperature sensor or DO membrane influences readings). The accuracy bar and the fact that temperature 'calibration' is verification rather than adjustment are only in A6.1 (t-verified-multiparam-accuracy-01: plus/minus 0.2 C when the sensor corrects another parameter; t-temp-cal-differs-01; t-temp-master-variable-01). The cadence is in A6.4 (ph-temp-sensor-annual-cal-01: at least annually, per A6.1) and the traceability requirement in A6.8 (mp-t4-nist-thermometer-02, which ties the same thermometer to the barometer used for DO calibration). Turn 2 cannot be answered from the EPA SOP and turn 1's dependency list is not stated in one place in the USGS chapters, so the pair needs both bodies. Also picks up the sensor-location point from A6.4 (ph-sensor-location-difference-01): on a multiparameter instrument the temperature sensor usually sits somewhere other than the pH electrode. Predicted rag: the slice says temperature is the master variable but says nothing about sensor verification, tolerance, or which readings a drifting thermistor corrupts.

turns.content: If the temperature sensor on one of our pods has gone off by half a degree and nobody noticed, which of the other readings are wrong because of it?

must_contain: states that the pH, dissolved oxygen, specific conductance and ORP channels all depend on the temperature sensor, so all of them are affected
explains for specific conductance that the reported value is a temperature-corrected number computed from the measured temperature
explains for dissolved oxygen that the reported concentration is computed from the sensor signal together with temperature
explains for pH that temperature affects the electrode slope and the buffer values used to calibrate it
explains for ORP that the reference potential the reading is set against is itself temperature dependent
notes that on a multiparameter instrument the temperature sensor typically sits in a different part of the instrument from the pH electrode
must_not: says only the temperature channel is affected
invents a numeric error propagated into a specific channel
answers from the probe datasheets instead of the field manuals

turns.content: So how do I keep that from happening — do I calibrate the temperature sensor like I do the pH one, and how often?

must_contain: states that a temperature sensor is not adjusted to a standard the way a pH or conductivity sensor is; the procedure is to verify its accuracy across the range of use
states the check is made against a NIST-certified or NIST-traceable thermometer
gives the required accuracy as within about plus or minus 0.2 C where the sensor is bundled on a multiparameter instrument and used to correct another parameter
gives the minimum cadence as at least annually
notes that the calibration solution must cover both the probe and the temperature sensor, and that moisture left on the temperature sensor can influence readings
must_not: describes adjusting the temperature sensor until it matches a reference
invents an accuracy tolerance or a check interval not in the manuals
states half a degree is within the requirement
